closed_issues.title: Relax the isinstance check of openphi.read_region() method
closed_issues.description:
Thanks for your work! Lately colleagues stumbled upon a convertibility difference between openslide and openphi when it comes to the read_region() method. OpenSlide appears to accept integral types such as numpy.int32 which fail the isinstance check at line openphi.py line 279 and 280. 
This matters when using other work written with openslide in mind such as CLAM (https://github.com/mahmoodlab/CLAM).
Do you think it makes sense to relax the isinstance check in order to align more with the openslide package?
E. g. checking against numbers.Integral instead of checking againt int.

Some testing shows compatibility with openslide when switching to checking against numbers.Integral for the datatypes:
np.int32, np.int64, np.uint32, np.uint64 (all work with openslide but not openphi)
and float, np.float32, np.float64 (neither work with openslide or openphi)

closed_issues.title: Add an openslide's function get_best_level_for_downsample. More compatible with openslide.
Open mode file
closed_issues.description:
Hello :smile: 

I'm the developer of the rust library [philips-isyntax-rs](https://github.com/AzHicham/philips-isyntax-rs)
I saw that you open a [IsyntaxFacade with "ficom" mode ](https://gitlab.com/BioimageInformaticsGroup/openphi/-/blob/master/openphi/openphi.py#L55) from my understanding, passing a empty string is equivalent to "caching-ficom" mode, see [here](https://github.com/AzHicham/philips-isyntax-rs/blob/3afb019138685404895a52461cc49d3c4de4d828/tests/test_pixel_engine.rs#L15) for all available open mode

The difference between the "ficom" and "caching-ficom" -> The latter creates a ".fic" file with header information and so enable fast re-opening file but that implies a RW permission -> so the issue is not about mounted volumes but about permissions.

However, I'm using the new SDK 2.0-L1 that runs under ubuntu 20.04 and not the SDK 2.0/ubuntu 18.04

Best Regards

closed_issues.title: read_region on downsampled levels fails with invalid coordinates
closed_issues.description: Make sure that the input coordinates are divisible by the downsampling factor of the level when attempting to read tiles.

closed_issues.title: openslide bounds are incorrect
closed_issues.description:
The properties openslide.bounds-x, openslide.bounds-y, openslide.bounds-width and openslide.bounds-height returned by OpenPhi are invalid in the sense that the described bounding box stretches outside the WSI.
The bounding box is also incorrect in the sense that it does not describe the minimal box that covers all scanned areas of the slide. In some cases I have seen, the returned bounding box fail to include large parts of the scanned area.

closed_issues.title: openslide.background-color contains empty string
closed_issues.description:
The openslide.background-color property is initialized with an emtpy string as value by default.
This is not how openslide works. When using openslide, this property always contain a valid color if it is defined.
